scenarios.name: Apollo 1 — Pad Fire
scenarios.description: Cabin pressurized to 16.7 psia with 100% O₂ during a plugs-out test. An electrical fault ignited materials that are marginal at sea level — the enriched atmosphere turned a spark into a flashover in seconds.
scenarios.lesson: Materials and wiring acceptable at 21% O₂ become aggressively flammable in enriched atmospheres — atmosphere control IS the fire policy.
scenarios.citation: Apollo 204 Review Board Final Report, NASA 1967

scenarios.name: Apollo 13 — Cryo Tank Rupture
scenarios.description: Damaged Teflon wire insulation inside a stirred liquid-oxygen tank ignited at ~1000 psi; the rupture cascaded into the adjacent tank and crippled life support across modules.
scenarios.lesson: Electrical faults inside pressurized oxidizer systems are ignitable bombs — thermal failure propagates to neighboring modules, not just the tank.

scenarios.name: Mir — Vika O₂ Generator Fire
scenarios.description: A solid-fuel oxygen generator (lithium perchlorate 'candle') ruptured and burned for ~14 minutes. The fire fed its own oxidizer — cutting ventilation did NOT extinguish it; crew needed masks, sector isolation and water cooling.
scenarios.lesson: Self-oxidizing chemical fires cannot be starved — they require isolation, cooling and crew respiratory protection until fuel is spent.
